title: Long ASML — Q2 Beat-and-Raise Confirms AI Lithography Supercycle
entry: $1,870–$1,940. Buy at the 9:31 AM ET open or any intraday pullback into the $1,870–$1,900 zone. ASML's Q2 beat (€9.3B vs €8.8B expected; EPS €7.59 vs €6.99 est; gross margin 54%) and 2026 guide raise (€43–45B, up from prior €37–40B) eliminates the bear case that AI semiconductor demand is rolling over. Do not chase above $1,940 on the initial post-earnings surge — earnings-gap stocks characteristically consolidate 3–5% intraday before resuming. If ASML opens above $1,960 on the U.S. open (implying >10% day-one gap), wait for a 3-day base to form before entering.
stop_loss: $1,790 daily close (~5.3% below $1,890 midpoint) — a daily close below the July 14 pre-earnings close of $1,775.64 would imply the post-earnings premium has been fully arbitraged away and the beat was already in the price. Below $1,790, the earnings catalyst is structurally exhausted regardless of the AI demand narrative.
targets: $2,050 — ASML sustains above $2,000 level as the market digests the raised 2026 guide and Q3 guide (€11–12B vs €10.37B consensus). 30Y UST stabilizes below 5.20% — even a mild rate normalization re-rates ASML's DCF 12–15%. The €43–45B full-year guide implies €11.5B average quarterly run rate — above the €10B prior consensus, forcing analyst upgrades across the sector. Buy-side models revise 2026 EPS estimates above €28. Cover 40% of position. +8.5% from $1,890 entry midpoint.

$2,200 — TSMC Q2 (July 16) confirms HBM4 and N2 node demand is on track — a direct demand read-through for ASML's EUV systems. The €43–45B 2026 guide requires ASML to ship approximately 15–18 High-NA EUV units vs the 7 shipped in 2025, and TSMC's capex plan confirms the purchase pipeline. European semis re-rate as the AI cycle narrative consolidates around lithography scarcity. Cover 40% of remaining position. +16.4% from entry.

$2,380 — Full AI supercycle confirmation: NVDA Q2 FY27 (August 26) raises Blackwell and Rubin GPU production targets beyond $130B revenue guidance; TSMC announces N2P tape-outs with ASML High-NA tooling; ASML backlog exceeds €60B (from current €48B). The final 20% position captures the multiple re-rating from a 35x to a 40x 2026 earnings scenario. +25.9% from entry.
catalyst: ASML Q2 2026 results confirmed pre-market July 15: €9.3B total net sales (+21.3% YoY, beat €8.8B consensus), EPS €7.59 (beat €6.99 est), gross margin 54% (at guide midpoint). 2026 full-year outlook raised to €43–45B from prior €37–40B range. Q3 2026 guide: €11–12B vs €10.37B consensus. This is the cleanest beat-and-raise in the AI semiconductor cycle — no caveats, no guidance hedging, no tariff risk flags. ASML is the monopoly supplier of EUV and High-NA EUV lithography systems; every advanced chip made for AI (NVDA Blackwell/Rubin, AMD MI300X+, Apple A-series, TSMC N2) requires ASML tooling. The raised guide eliminates the only remaining structural bear case for the AI hardware cycle.
thesis:
ASML's Q2 beat-and-raise is not incremental news — it is the elimination of the AI demand uncertainty that has been the primary overhang on semiconductor valuations since early 2026. The bear argument for the past 18 months has been: 'AI capex will slow; the hyperscalers are overbuilding; ASML's backlog will convert to order cancellations.' Today's results close that debate. €43–45B in 2026 revenue requires ASML to ship an unprecedented volume of EUV and High-Na EUV systems on a schedule that has already been committed to in customer purchase orders — these are not soft intentions but manufacturing capacity build-outs at TSMC, Samsung, and Intel that are years in construction.

The IBM enterprise software collapse (-25% July 14) is actually structurally bullish for ASML. IBM's CEO attributed the decline to enterprise customers reallocating IT budgets from software/consulting to AI hardware purchases — specifically GPU infrastructure. Every dollar diverted from SAP licenses and IBM consulting toward NVDA Blackwell racks translates directly into incremental TSMC wafer demand, which translates into incremental ASML tool orders with an 18–24 month lead time. The IBM read-through is a 2027–2028 demand signal for ASML, not a headwind.

The geopolitical risk that constrained ASML in 2023–2024 — Dutch export controls on EUV to China — has been partially resolved by the U.S.–China AI chip framework. ASML now ships older DUV systems (not EUV) to Chinese customers with end-user certificate verification, which represents approximately 15% of the original China revenue that was expected. More importantly, the raised €43–45B guide implies this China headwind is already factored in — the non-China demand (TSMC Taiwan/Arizona, Samsung Pyeongtaek, Intel Fab 34) is sufficient to hit the guide independently.

At $1,890 entry and a 2026 consensus EPS estimate revised to approximately €28–30 post-results, ASML trades at approximately 58x 2026 earnings — elevated but defensible for a monopoly infrastructure asset with a €48B+ backlog providing 3+ years of revenue visibility. The stop at $1,790 limits downside to 5.3% while the target range of $2,050–$2,380 reflects 8–26% upside — a favorable asymmetry for a quality compounder that just eliminated its primary risk factor.
bull_case: TSMC Q2 (July 16) confirms N2 node ramp is on schedule and raises 2026 capex guidance — a direct ASML tool demand confirmation. NVDA Q2 FY27 (August 26) raises Blackwell revenue targets above $130B. ASML's Q3 results in October confirm the raised guide on track. The combination of three consecutive AI infrastructure confirmation beats drives ASML to $2,200–$2,380 before September.
bear_case: WTI breaks above $80 (Iran Hormuz trip wire), embedding oil into August CPI and raising September Fed hike probability above 65%. A confirmed September hike compresses all long-duration assets including ASML's 58x earnings multiple. Simultaneously, TSMC Q2 (July 16) disappoints on H2 guidance, signaling the capex front-loading that occurred in H1 will not repeat in H2 — reducing ASML's near-term order inflow. In this scenario, ASML retraces to $1,790–$1,820 as rate and demand headwinds combine.
invalidation: $1,790 ASML daily close (below pre-earnings July 14 close, implying full earnings premium erasure); OR TSMC Q2 (July 16) guides H2 2026 capex below $20B — would reduce ASML EUV tool deliveries in H2; OR September Fed hike probability rises above 70% post-PPI/Warsh and ASML's P/E compresses below 50x on rate fears; OR ASML management revises the €43–45B guide downward at the Q3 update (October 2026) citing Hormuz-related supply chain disruption to photoresist or specialty chemical inputs.
